usdRate.note: DKK 668.95 per USD 100; World Bank 2025 average 6.62.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Danmarks Statistik, PRIS01 consumer price index (annual change)
inflation_cpi.note: CPI up 2.2% year on year in September 2026 (2.0% in August); World Bank 2025 average 1.9%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: Krone pegged to the euro (ECB 2% target); Danish CPI 2021-2025 average 3.2%, 1.9% in 2025
inflation_projection.note: The fixed-exchange-rate policy ties Danish inflation to the euro area, so the ECB 2% target is used; recent years outside the 2022 spike were close to 2%.

policy_rate.note: Current-account and certificates-of-deposit rate 2.10%, lending rate 2.25%; raised from 1.85% in early September 2026 alongside the ECB.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: Danmarks Nationalbank MFI statistics (DNRUIPI): household transferable (on-demand) deposits in DKK, outstanding
savings_account_rate.note: Average 0.40% on households' on-demand DKK deposits; deposits with notice paid 1.21%.

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: Danmarks Nationalbank MFI statistics (DNRNIPI): new household time deposits in DKK, up to 3 months
fdr_3m_rate.note: New business effective rate, September 2026 (1.48% in August).

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: Danmarks Nationalbank MFI statistics (DNRNIPI): new household time deposits in DKK, over 3 months up to 1 year
fdr_1y_rate.note: New business effective rate, September 2026; 1-2 years paid 2.23%.

dps_rate.note: Danish banks do not offer a standard monthly recurring deposit product with a published rate; regular saving goes into ordinary or notice savings accounts or tax-favoured schemes (aldersopsparing, børneopsparing).

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: Danmarks Nationalbank MFI statistics (DNRUIPI): all household DKK deposits, outstanding
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Average effective rate on all outstanding household deposits in DKK; World Bank FR.INR.DPST has no Denmark figure.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Denmark has no retail government savings certificate or savings bond sold to individuals; government bonds are bought through banks on the market.

tbill_91d_rate.note: Treasury bills (skatkammerbeviser) are issued by Danmarks Nationalbank for the state, but no current 3-month yield could be read; worldgovernmentbonds.com loads yields by script.

tbond_5y_rate.note: No current 5-year Danish government bond yield was found: Trading Economics shows only 2- and 10-year yields and worldgovernmentbonds.com could not be read.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Trading Economics, Denmark 10-year government bond yield
tbond_10y_rate.note: ECB long-term convergence yield for Denmark was 3.29% in September 2026; the 2-year yield was 2.79%.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Denmark taxes on personal income
tax_bank_interest.note: No final withholding: interest is positive net capital income, taxed at average municipal tax 25.05% plus bottom tax 12.01% (about 37%), up to 42% for high incomes.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No retail government savings certificate exists; interest on government bonds is taxed as ordinary capital income (about 37-42%).

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Finansiel Stabilitet, Garantiformuen (Danish deposit guarantee scheme)
deposit_insurance_limit.note: Cover is the equivalent of EUR 100,000 per depositor per institution, converted at the ECB rate of DKK 7.4735 per euro (30 Oct 2026); EUR 150,000 for 6 months after life events, pension savings fully covered.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: Danish law caps the cost of consumer credit (annual percentage rate ceiling), but the statutory text on retsinformation.dk could not be read; Nationalbanken's credit-card interest series for households is confidential ('..'). Overdrafts and revolving credit to households averaged 4.62% in September 2026.

equity_return_low.sourceName: Copenhagen stock index 1,633 on 30 Oct 2026, 45% below its June 2024 high of 2,967
equity_return_low.note: Low case: Danish shares, concentrated in a few large health-care and shipping companies, return little more than safe deposits.

equity_return_base.sourceName: Copenhagen index (Trading Economics); 1-year deposit 1.96% less 37% tax = 1.2%
equity_return_base.note: Base capped near the after-tax safe rate plus about 4 points because the index has fallen sharply since 2024 and depends on a handful of companies.

equity_return_high.sourceName: Copenhagen index; long-run global equity returns
equity_return_high.note: High case: a diversified equity fund matching long-run global equity returns of about 7% in kroner.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); DKK pegged to the euro
gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold barely keeps up after the 2025-26 spike, with no help from the krone.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); ECB 2% inflation target
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises roughly with world inflation plus a little, and the krone (pegged to the euro) is assumed stable against the dollar.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in krone terms.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Household notice deposits 1.21% less 37% capital income tax (Nationalbanken DNRUIPI)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: easy-access savings after tax, with rates drifting lower.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: New household deposits 3-12 months 1.96% less 37% tax = 1.2% (Nationalbanken DNRNIPI)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: after-tax 1-year term deposit rate.

fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: holding long government or mortgage bonds after tax.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: Finanstilsynet and Forsikring & Pension do not publish an industry-wide life claim settlement ratio that could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover (risikolivsforsikring) is sold, mostly through labour-market pension schemes, but no published premium table per DKK 1,000 of cover was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Hospital treatment is free at the point of use in the public regional hospitals; no official figure for the out-of-pocket cost of a private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: Private health insurance (sundhedsforsikring) is mostly an employer benefit with flat premiums, not priced per DKK 100,000 of cover; no published premium table was found.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Danmarks Statistik PRIS01, health (COICOP 06): +1.4% year on year in September 2026
goal_inflation_health.note: Measured health prices rise slowly because most care is public and free, but private dental, physiotherapy and medicine costs are planned at 3%, a point above headline inflation.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Danmarks Statistik PRIS01, education (COICOP 10): +4.1% year on year in September 2026
goal_inflation_education.note: Public education is free; the fees people do pay (private schools, courses) are rising about 4% a year, which is used for planning.

life_expectancy.note: Danmarks Statistik life table 2024-2025 (HISB8): men 80.25, women 83.90.

life_table_remaining.note: Official tables are by sex only; total is the simple average of men and women.

support_ratio.note: People aged 15-64 divided by people 65+ in the official 2026 projection; World Bank 2025 old-age dependency 33.4 gives 3.0.

retirement_age_default.note: Folkepension age is 67 for people born 1 July 1955 to 31 December 1962, then 68 (born 1963-66), 69 (1967-70) and 70 (born 1971 or later); same for men and women.

retirement_age_government.note: Most public employees are on ordinary contracts and follow the folkepension age; the separate retirement rule for tenured civil servants (tjenestemænd) could not be confirmed from a readable official source.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case: easy-access savings after tax.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: New household deposits 3-12 months 1.96% less 37% tax = 1.2%
retirement_return_base.note: Base case capped at the after-tax 1-year term deposit rate.

retirement_return_high.note: High case: a ladder of longer government and mortgage bonds after tax, slightly below the 10-year yield.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 5% and half safe fixed income at about 1.2-2% after tax.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Basic amount of the residence-based folkepension, DKK 7,544 a month before tax in 2026; a means-tested pension supplement adds up to DKK 8,729 (single) or 4,467 (couple).

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: borger.dk, folkepension (age, residence and income rules)
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Not contributory: needs Danish citizenship or 10 years' residence between 15 and pension age (full rate after 40 years). The basic amount is not reduced by other income; only the supplement is income-tested.

gratuity_rule.note: No per-year gratuity: the Salaried Employees Act (funktionærloven s.2a) gives a lump severance of 1, 2 or 3 months' pay after 12, 15 or 18 years of service, which does not fit a days-per-year rule; holiday pay is separate.

public_pension_scheme.note: Two public tiers: the residence-based folkepension and the compulsory ATP lifetime pension (contributions from age 16, one-third employee, two-thirds employer, paid from pension age, can be deferred 10 years). Folkepension is adjusted yearly by the rate-adjustment percentage; both are taxed as income.

dps.note: No standard recurring-deposit product; regular saving goes into savings accounts or tax-favoured schemes.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No retail government savings certificate or bond sold directly to individuals.

tbill_91d.note: Issued for the state by Danmarks Nationalbank, mainly to institutions.

equity_fund.note: Retail investment funds are widely available; gains taxed as share income (27%/42%), or 17% inside an aktiesparekonto.

gold.note: No restriction on buying physical gold.

pensionScheme.name: ATP Livslang Pension
pensionScheme.note: Compulsory supplementary lifetime pension alongside the folkepension.

oldAgeAllowance.name: Folkepension (state pension, paid by Udbetaling Danmark)

publicHealthCover.name: Public health insurance (sygesikring), regional health services
